Hook System Posts Taxonomies Five Building Blocks of WP Development

Taxonomies are used to classify our posts Categories and Tags ship with WordPress ○ Categories are hierarchical ○ Tags are not Posts can be associated with categories or tags You can also create custom taxonomies within WordPress, that are / are not hierarchical to tag content more appropriately Taxonomies can be used to query posts directly Taxonomies Fancy word for categories
Hook System Posts Taxonomies Meta Five Building Blocks of WP Development

Meta is where a lot of the developer power is in WP Meta is custom data that lives in the database that is associated with a post in what is essentially a key/value store Meta is not limited to being associated with posts, but can also be associated with taxonomies, and users as well Meta Key / Value data store for Posts

Add ○ add_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’, $value ) Update ○ update_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’, $value ) ○ update_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’, $value, $previous_value ) Delete ○ delete_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’ ) ○ delete_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’, $value ) Retrieve ○ get_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’ ) Meta Programmatically adding to posts

Meta, by default, is returned as an array. If your architecture only holds a single value for a key, then you need to specify that when you get meta ○ get_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’ ) [ results ] ○ get_post_meta( $post_id, ‘key’, true ) result Meta Quick note!
Meta Options Sitewide meta are known as “options” ○ Options set with an expiration are known as “transients” ○ Follows key / value approach ○ Doesn’t follow the array approach
